newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Impexmetal debut seen with limited upside.
newsitem.headline: Polish Impexmetal debut seen with limited upside.

text.p: Polish metals trader Impexmetal SA is seen starting trade on the main market of the Warsaw bourse on Tuesday no more than 20 percent higher than its public offering price of 36 zlotys, analysts said on Monday.
Analysts said relatively weak financial ratios and a bourse debut coming just before that of Bank Handlowy and copper giant KGHM, two of Poland's largest firms, would dampen buying.

"The average p/e for (Polish) trading conglomerates over the past 12 months is around 15, and 18.5 for Impexmetal at the (36-zloty) offering price, is too big a premium " said Jacek Mazur, an analyst at Bank Pekao SA brokerage.
Mazur said Impexmetal could start trade virtually flat and stay that way in coming weeks, performing roughly in line with the overall market.
Entering bourse trade will be the 3,189,171 shares of the firm's April public offering and 6,325,190 series A shares, 2,994,142 of which the state sold in May at the same price.
In the public offer 3.6 million shares were subscribed and underwriter Nomura International Plc took 1.6 million.

Analysts said that despite the stock's limited debut potential Impexmetal could benefit in the longer term from its plans to shift toward production from trade by adding firms to its holding, and its diversification from steel.
They said the latter move had shielded the firm somewhat from the risky metal industry ever dependent on prices.

"It's such a volatile market, though it's not as risky as only relying on steel, which can really be subject to political pressure... so from that point of view it's more attractive than a typical steel company," said Jacek Dzierwa of Salomon Brothers in London.

Dzierwa was bullish on the firm's participation in the consortium to build the 364-km A-2 motorway in the west of the country but noted the firm's gradual shift from trade toward production itself implied risk.
Impexmetal lifted January-May net profit this year to 4.6 million zlotys on sales of 589.5 million from 4.3 million zlotys in the same period last year on sales of 565.5 million.
The firm made a group profit last year of 103.2 million zlotys on sales of 1.8 billion zlotys.
